en.name: Agatha
en.summary: Sicilian virgin martyr of the third century whose torture, including mutilation, made her one of the most venerated early women martyrs.
en.body: Agatha was a young Sicilian noblewoman who had consecrated her virginity to God when a powerful Roman official, Quintianus, sought to force her into marriage or concubinage and, when she consistently refused, denounced her Christian faith to the authorities during the persecution of Emperor Decius. According to the tradition recorded in her early acts, she was subjected to severe torture, including having her breasts cut off, and was reportedly comforted and healed in prison by a vision of the Apostle Peter before dying of her injuries around 251. Her feast became one of the most significant in Sicily, where legend holds her intercession has repeatedly protected Catania from eruptions of nearby Mount Etna, and her veil is still processed toward the volcano's lava flows during eruptions according to long local custom. She is named among the women commemorated in the Roman Canon of the Mass and remains one of the most widely venerated virgin martyrs of the early Church.

fr.name: Agathe
fr.summary: Jeune martyre sicilienne du IIIe siècle, vénérée depuis l'Antiquité comme protectrice contre les incendies et les éruptions volcaniques.
fr.body: Agathe était une jeune femme d'une famille sicilienne noble qui, selon la tradition, avait consacré sa virginité à Dieu et repoussa les avances d'un gouverneur romain, lequel la dénonça alors comme chrétienne durant la persécution de Dèce. Elle subit des tortures particulièrement cruelles, dont la mutilation de sa poitrine, avant de mourir en prison vers 251. Son culte se répandit rapidement en Sicile et au-delà, et sa protection contre le feu, notamment les éruptions de l'Etna, devint un aspect central de sa vénération populaire, son voile étant traditionnellement porté en procession pour apaiser les éruptions volcaniques. Elle est comptée parmi les vierges martyres les plus vénérées de l'Église primitive et son nom figure dans le Canon romain de la messe.
